newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan invites HK leader Tung to visit.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan invites HK leader Tung to visit.

text.p: Taiwan Vice President Lien Chan on Monday invited Hong Kong's Beijing-appointed leader Tung Chee-hwa to visit the Nationalist-ruled island and said he was willing to visit anywhere in rival China, including Hong Kong.
"We welcome him to visit the Republic of China (on Taiwan)," Lien told Hong Kong's Chinese Television News minutes before the British colony's handover to Chinese sovereignty.

The elected vice president, who doubles as premier or cabinet chief, said he was willing to visit anywhere in the communist mainland "with no preconditions, and that Chinese mainland of course will include Hong Kong".
Beijing has said leaders of Taiwan's exiled Republic of China could visit in principle, but only in their capacity as Nationalist Party leaders, not government officials.

Lien, interviewed in Taipei, again rejected reunification with the mainland under the "one country, two systems" formula of local autonomy that Beijing pledges to implement in Hong Kong, saying mainland first must undergo democratisation.
"We are a democratic country. We must respect the wishes of hte people. We cannot use their welfare as bargaining chips in a negotiating or dealmaking," Lien said.

Coining a new twist on Beijing's proposed formula, Lien said union across the Taiwan strait would be possible only under conditions of "one country, one good system" -- saying this could only be multiparty democracy.
